q: 71. The rocks formed due to solidification of molten mass laying below or above the earth surface are called .....
explain: Rocks formed by cooling and solidification of molten magma, either below (intrusive) or on (extrusive) the earth's surface, are igneous rocks.

q: 72. The sedimentary rocks are formed due to .....
options: solidification of molten mass lying below or above the earth surface
gradual deposition of materials like sand, clay, etc., generally by setting water
alteration of original structure under heat and excessive pressure
explain: Sedimentary rocks form by gradual deposition and consolidation of materials like sand and clay, generally settled by water.

q: 73. Spalling hammer is used for .....
explain: A spalling hammer is a heavy hammer used for rough dressing, i.e. removing large irregular parts of a quarried stone.

q: 74. The yield strength and tensile strength of low carbon steel may be improved by the addition of .....
explain: As per the answer key, vanadium. It refines grain and raises yield and tensile strength of low carbon steel.

q: 75. German silver is an alloy of .....
explain: German silver contains no silver; it is an alloy of copper, nickel and zinc. Options c and d are identical in the book, and the key gives c.

q: 76. PVC stands for .....
explain: PVC is polyvinyl chloride. Option b is the closest to this in the book, and the key gives b.

q: 77. Stainless steel resists corrosion due to .....
explain: Chromium forms a thin, stable oxide film on the surface that protects the steel from corrosion.

q: 78. Brass is an alloy of .....
explain: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.

q: 79. The rocks which are formed due to cooling of magma at considerable depth from earth's surface are called .....
explain: Magma cooling slowly at great depth forms coarse-grained plutonic rocks such as granite.

q: 80. The rocks which are formed due to cooling of magma at a relatively shallow depth from the earth's surface is called .....
explain: Cooling at shallow depth gives hypabyssal rocks, such as dolerite.

q: 81. The rocks which are formed due to pouring of magma at the earth's surface are called .....
explain: Lava cooling quickly on the surface gives fine-grained volcanic (extrusive) rocks such as basalt.

q: 82. Pick up the plutonic rock from the following .....
explain: Granite is the plutonic rock; dolerite is hypabyssal and basalt is volcanic.

q: 83. Pick up the hypabyssal rock from the following .....
explain: Dolerite forms at shallow depth, so it is hypabyssal.

q: 84. Pick up the volcanic rock from the following .....
explain: Basalt forms from lava poured on the surface, so it is volcanic.

q: 85. The rocks in which argil (or clay) pre-dominates, are called .....
explain: Rocks in which clay (argil) predominates are argillaceous rocks, for example slate and laterite.

q: 86. In a rock calcium carbonate pre-dominates. State whether it is .....
explain: Rocks in which calcium carbonate predominates are calcareous rocks, such as limestone and marble.

q: 87. The quarrying of stone by the method of wedging is successfully carried out in .....
explain: Wedging works well in soft, stratified rocks such as sandstone, limestone and marble.

q: 88. The solution of salts from the soil absorbed by the trees which becomes a viscous solution due to loss of moisture and action of carbon dioxide is known as .....
explain: The solution of salts absorbed from the soil, which thickens as moisture is lost and CO2 acts on it, is sap.

q: 89. The age of the tree can be judged from .....
explain: One annual ring is added each year, so counting them gives the age of the tree.

q: 90. The best primer used for structural steel work is .....
explain: Red lead is anti-corrosive, so it is the best primer for structural steel.

q: 91. The vehicle used in bronze paints is usually .....
explain: Bronze paint uses nitro-cellulose lacquer as the vehicle for the metallic powder.

q: 92. The aggregate is called fine aggregate if it is completely retained on .....
explain: As per the answer key, option a. Note: fine aggregate is usually defined as passing 4.75 mm and retained on 0.15 mm, so the wording in the book is loose.

q: 93. The aggregate is called coarse aggregate if it is completely retained on .....
explain: Aggregate retained on the 4.75 mm IS sieve is coarse aggregate. (The book prints option d with an 's)' label.)

q: 94. The bulking of sand is due to .....
options: the increase in space between the particles, caused by the surface tension effect of moisture
the swelling of air in voids
explain: A thin film of moisture around sand particles pushes them apart through surface tension, increasing the volume (bulking).

q: 95. The cement mortar mix generally used for masonry work is .....
explain: As per the answer key, a 1:6 cement-sand mortar is generally used for masonry work.

q: 96. The cement mortar mix generally used for internal plastering is .....
explain: As per the answer key, a 1:5 mix is generally used for internal plastering.

q: 97. The pigment used in paints for corrosive resistance, is .....
explain: Red lead is a rust-inhibiting pigment, so it is used where corrosion resistance is needed.

q: 98. The material generally not used as extender in paints is .....
explain: Silica, gypsum and talc are extenders (inert fillers). Zinc white is a pigment (base), not an extender.

q: 99. The commonly used thinner in oil paints, is .....
explain: Both naphtha and turpentine are commonly used thinners for oil paints.

q: 100. Spirit varnish generally consists of .....
explain: Spirit varnish is shellac dissolved in spirit (alcohol). Option d is a misprint of 'spirit and shellac', and it is the one the key gives.

q: 101. Oil varnish generally consists of .....
explain: Oil varnish is made by dissolving resin in linseed oil and turpentine.

q: 102. Bitumen paints offer .....
explain: Bitumen paints give a black protective, water-resistant coating rather than a decorative one.

q: 103. Stucco are suitable for .....
explain: Stucco is a plaster finish that can be applied on both stone masonry and brick walls.

q: 104. Wrought iron contains carbon upto .....
explain: Wrought iron is almost pure iron with carbon up to about 0.15%.

q: 105. Wrought iron is manufactured from pig iron by .....
explain: Wrought iron is produced from pig iron through refining, puddling and shingling, so all are correct.

q: 106. Forge pig may be converted to wrought iron by .....
explain: Forge (white) pig iron is converted to wrought iron by puddling in a reverberatory furnace.

q: 107. Brittleness of cold is due to an excess of .....
explain: Excess phosphorus makes iron brittle when cold (cold shortness).

q: 108. Red short iron cracks when bent due to the presence of .....
explain: Excess sulphur makes iron brittle at red heat (red shortness).

q: 109. The process of decarbonising the pig iron completely and then adding proper percentage of carbon for manufacturing steel is called .....
explain: As per the answer key, option a. Note: this description usually matches the Bessemer or open hearth process, so the key answer looks doubtful.

q: 110. In arches stratified stones are placed so that their planes are .....
explain: In an arch, the bedding planes of stratified stones are placed radial to the curve so the thrust acts perpendicular to the beds.

q: 111. The tendency of a stone is, to split along .....
explain: Cleavage is the tendency to split along definite planes.

q: 112. The size of modular bricks, is .....
explain: The standard modular brick is 19 × 9 × 9 cm (19.0 cm length, and with mortar 20 × 10 × 10 cm).

q: 113. The term frog means .....
options: an apparatus to lift the stone
a depression on a face of brick
vertical joint in a brick work
explain: A frog is the depression on a face of the brick that holds mortar for a better key.

q: 114. Pegmatite is a/an .....
explain: Pegmatite is a very coarse-grained intrusive igneous rock.

q: 115. Which of the following ingredients of the brick earth enables the brick to retain its shape?
explain: Silica prevents cracking, shrinkage and warping and helps the brick retain its shape.

q: 116. The process of mixing clay, water and other ingredients to make brick is known as .....
explain: As per the answer key, kneading. Note: other questions in the book use 'pugging' or 'tempering' for the same operation.

q: 117. Dolomite is a lime stone which contains carbonate of magnesia upto .....
explain: As per the answer key, dolomite limestone contains up to about 45% magnesium carbonate.

q: 118. Ultimate strength to cement is provided by .....
explain: Dicalcium silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly and is responsible for the later (ultimate) strength.

q: 119. To retard the initial setting time of cement, the compound responsible, is .....
explain: Gypsum is added (about 2 to 3%) to control the quick setting caused by C3A.

q: 120. The compound of Portland cement which reacts immediately with water and also sets first is .....
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts instantly with water and causes flash set.

q: 121. When quarrying is to be done in hard stone and compact rocks, the usual method of quarrying is .....
explain: Hard and compact rocks cannot be removed by wedging or channelling, so blasting is used.

q: 122. The most powerful explosive used in blasting is .....
explain: As per the answer key, gun cotton is the most powerful of the options.

q: 123. The dressing of stone is done .....
explain: As per the answer key, dressing is done immediately after quarrying, while the stone still contains quarry sap and is soft.

q: 124. The crushing strength of a stone depends upon its .....
explain: Crushing strength depends on texture and specific gravity (density).

q: 125. The percentage of alumina in a good brick clay should vary from .....
explain: Good brick earth contains about 20 to 30% alumina, which gives plasticity.

q: 126. Monel metal is an alloy of .....
explain: Monel metal is mainly nickel (about 67%) and copper (about 30%).

q: 127. The proportions of copper and zinc in Muntz metal are .....
explain: Muntz metal is 60% copper and 40% zinc.

q: 128. The main ingredient in the manufacture of glass is .....
explain: Silica (sand) is the main constituent of glass.

q: 129. The type of glass used for the window of bath room and toilets is .....
explain: Ground (frosted) glass is translucent, giving light with privacy.

q: 130. The type of glass used in glazing the north light trusses is .....
explain: Wired glass is strong and holds together if broken, so it is used for north light glazing.

q: 131. Asphalt is a mixture of .....
explain: Asphalt is bitumen mixed with inert mineral matter.

q: 132. The asbestos content in asbestos cement sheets is roughly about .....
explain: As per the answer key, asbestos cement sheets contain roughly 15% asbestos.

q: 133. The type of glass used to make laboratory equipment and cooking utensils is .....
explain: Borosilicate glass has high heat and chemical resistance, so it is used for lab ware and cookware.

q: 134. Water glass is .....
options: water formed by condensation on glass
solution of sodium silicate in water
explain: Water glass is a solution of sodium silicate in water.

q: 135. The base metal in Y-alloy is .....
explain: Y-alloy is an aluminium-based alloy containing copper, nickel and magnesium.

q: 136. Shingle is .....
explain: Shingle is rounded pebbles worn by water action.

q: 137. The silica in Portland cement should be .....
explain: Portland cement contains about 20 to 25% silica.

q: 138. The dry process of mixing is usually employed in the manufacture of Portland cement when the raw material is .....
explain: As per the answer key, option b. Note: this answer was one of the less legible key entries, and the dry process is usually associated with hard raw materials such as limestone and shale.

q: 139. The process of manufacturing steel by heating short lengths of wrought iron bars mixed with charcoal in the clay crucibles and collecting the molten iron into moulds, is known as .....
explain: Melting wrought iron with charcoal in clay crucibles and casting it is the crucible process.

q: 140. Bessemer process is used for the manufacture of .....
explain: The Bessemer process converts molten pig iron into steel by blowing air through it.
